# Authors: Maayan Malter, Sonia Kim, Janet Metcalfe (Final Code Update: Oct 12, 2020)

# Install and load packages
```{r, packages}
library('easypackages')
packages(c('devtools', 'corrr', 'psych', 'car', 'dplyr', 'sjstats', 'lsr', 'DescTools', 
           'lsmeans', 'effsize', 'lme4', 'lmerTest', 'tidyverse', 'janitor', 'here', 
           'tidyr', 'stringr', 'effects', 'ggplot2'))
```
# Create a theme to make APA style graphs
```{r, theme}
apatheme=theme_bw()+
  theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
        panel.border=element_blank(),
        axis.line=element_line(),
        text=element_text(family='Times'))
```

# Experiment 1: Main effect of Agency
## Load the data
```{r, data1}
study1 <- read_csv(here::here("1morality.csv")) %>%
  clean_names %>%
  glimpse()
```
## Demographics
```{r, demographics1}
mean(study1$age)
sd(study1$age)
table(study1$gender)
```
## Create dictionary of codes
### Agency (0: Noagency, 1: Agency)
### Decision Type (0: Deontological, 1: Utilitarian)
### Attention (0: Not paying attention, 1: Paying attention)
### Recall (0: Can’t recall, 1: Can recall)
### Redo (0: identically, 1: differently)
### Time for Experiment 2 (0: Immediate, 1: Time lag)

## Create categorical variable for conditions
```{r, categorical1}
# Agency
study1$agency <- factor(study1$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(study1$agency)
table(study1$agency)
# Decision
study1$decision <- factor(study1$decision, labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(study1$decision)
table(study1$decision)
```


## Moral culpability score
### See how well the five items hold together
```{r, alphafive1}
# Cronbach's alpha for all five questions
allfive <- as.matrix(cbind(study1$feel, study1$upset, study1$responsible, 
                           study1$guilty, study1$regret))
psych::alpha(allfive, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
summary(allfive)
```
### If we drop feel and keep upset:
```{r, alphafour1}
fourq <- as.matrix(cbind(study1$upset, study1$responsible, study1$guilty, study1$regret))
psych::alpha(fourq, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```
### If we also drop upset:
```{r, alphathree1}
threecog <- as.matrix(cbind(study1$responsible, study1$guilty, study1$regret))
psych::alpha(threecog, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```
### This gives us the highest alpha and conceptually groups the more cognitive questions about moral culpability together and the questions about affective responses together.
### Thus we create a variable 'moral' which is the average of the three items retained (done in the data file)

## Means, SDs, and ANOVAs for each item individually
### (1) General Feelings (higher score means more positive)
```{r, feel1}
# mean and sd
group_by(study1, study1$decision, study1$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(feel, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(feel, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# anova
feel1dv.aov <- aov(feel ~ agency*decision, data = study1)
Anova(feel1dv.aov)
# effect size
etaSquared(feel1dv.aov, type = 3, anova = FALSE) 
# post hoc scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(feel ~ agency*decision, data = study1), method = "scheffe", 
            conf.level = .95)

# plot
Feel1Plot <- ggplot(study1, aes(x=decision, y=feel, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
Feel1Plot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Programming Type", y = "Feelings", fill = "agency", 
       title = "General Feelings about Programming the Car") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```

## ANOVA for aggregate scores
### ANOVAs for five-item aggregate and four-item aggregate
```{r, fivefour}
study1$aggfive <- (study1$feel + study1$upset + study1$responsible + study1$guilty 
                   + study1$regret)/5
fivedv.aov <- aov(aggfive ~ agency*decision, data = study1)
Anova(fivedv.aov, type = "III")

study1$aggfour <- (study1$upset + study1$responsible + study1$guilty + study1$regret)/4
fourdv.aov <- aov(aggfour ~ agency*decision, data = study1)
Anova(fourdv.aov, type = "III")
```
#### We also did this in excel so there is a variable named "moral" that is the exact same as this variable named "threeitem" and therefore either are fine to use in analyses and will have the same results.
```{r}
# average of the three
threeitem <- (study1$responsible + study1$guilty + study1$regret)/3
```
### Main analysis of moral culpability 
#### Means, SDs, ANOVA, partial eta squared (effect size), Post Hoc Scheffe test, plot 
```{r, moral1}
# mean and sd
group_by(study1, study1$agency, study1$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# anova
moral1dv.aov <- aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = study1)
Anova(moral1dv.aov, type = "III")
# effect size
etaSquared(moral1dv.aov, type = 3, anova = TRUE) 
# post hoc scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = study1), method = "scheffe", 
            conf.level = .95)

# plot
Moral1Plot <- ggplot(study1, aes(x=decision, y=moral, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
Moral1Plot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Programming Type", y = "Moral Culpability", fill = "Agency", 
       title = "Moral Culpability") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```

## Logistic regression for redo
### Redo: Whether they would program the car differently when they have a chance to do it over.
```{r, redo1}
# For variable 'redo', 0 means they would program it the same 
# while 1 means they would program differently.
redoreg <- glm(redo ~ agency*decision, family = "binomial", data = study1)
summary(redoreg)
```

# Experiment 2: Replication and inclusion of temporal distance

## Load data
```{r, data2}
study2 <- read_csv(here::here("2moralitytime.csv")) %>%
  clean_names %>%
  glimpse()
```

## Demographics
```{r, demographics2}
mean(study2$age)
sd(study2$age)
table(study2$gen)
```

## Make categorical variables
```{r, categorical2}
# Agency
study2$agency <- factor(study2$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(study2$agency)
table(study2$agency)
# Decision
study2$decision <- factor(study2$decision, labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(study2$decision)
table(study2$decision)
# Temporal
study2$temporal <- factor(study2$temporal, labels = c("Immediate", "Five Years"))
is.factor(study2$temporal)
table(study2$temporal)
```

## Cronbach's alpha for three items
```{r, alphathree2}
timecog <- as.matrix(cbind(study2$responsible, study2$guilty, study2$regret))
psych::alpha(timecog, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10, na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```
## Marginal means and full factorial means for moral culpability
```{r, means2}
group_by(study2, study2$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study2, study2$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study2, study2$temporal) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study2, study2$decision, study2$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study2, study2$temporal, study2$decision, study2$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
## ANOVA for moral culpability
```{r, moral2}
#anova
moral2dv.aov <- aov(moral ~ agency*decision*temporal, data = study2)
Anova(moral2dv.aov, type = "III")
# effect size
etaSquared(moral2dv.aov, type = 3, anova = FALSE) # Effect size
# post hoc scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = study2), method = "hsd", 
            conf.level = .95)
```


## ANOVA for individual items
```{r}
#General Feelings
feel2dv.aov <- aov(feel~ agency*decision*temporal, data = study2)
Anova(feel2dv.aov, type = "III")

#Upset
upset2dv.aov <- aov(upset ~ agency*decision*temporal, data = study2)
Anova(upset2dv.aov, type = "III")

#Responsibility
res2dv.aov <- aov(responsible ~ agency*decision*temporal, data = study2)
Anova(res2dv.aov, type = "III")

#Guilt
guilt2dv.aov <- aov(guilty ~ agency*decision*temporal, data = study2)
Anova(guilt2dv.aov, type = "III")

#Regret
regret2dv.aov <- aov(regret ~ agency*decision*temporal, data = study2)
Anova(regret2dv.aov, type = "III")
```


# Experiment 3: Predictions of other people's feelings (within-subjects)

## Load data
## We have the original data as "3moralitypredict.csv" while we use the identical data in long-format for the purpose of this analyses, with the name "3moralitypredict2.csv"
```{r, data3}
study3 <- read_csv(here::here("3moralitypredict2.csv")) %>%
  clean_names %>%
  glimpse()
```
### Data must be in long format and was cleaned and organized in excel although this could also be done using the dplyr package.

## Means and SDs
```{r, means3}
group_by(study3, agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

## Paired t-test
```{r, ttest3}
pairt <- t.test(moral ~ agency, data = study3, paired = TRUE)
pairt
```

## Alternatively we can do this analysis with a linear mixed effects regression (LMER, with the lmerTest package)
```{r, lmertest3}
result<-lmer(moral ~ agency + (1|id), data = study3)
summary(result)
```

## Cohen's D effect size
```{r, effectsize3}
cohen.d(study3$moral, study3$agency, pooled=TRUE, paired=TRUE, na.rm=FALSE,
        hedges.correction = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, noncentral = FALSE)
```

## LMER tests for each item
```{r}
# responsibility
reslmer<-lmer(responsible ~ agency + (1|id), data = study3)
summary(reslmer)

# guilt
guiltlmer<-lmer(guilty ~ agency + (1|id), data = study3)
summary(guiltlmer)

# regret
regretlmer<-lmer(regret ~ agency + (1|id), data = study3)
summary(regretlmer)
```

## Load data
```{r, data4}
study4 <- read_csv(here::here("4moralitythirdperson.csv")) %>%
  clean_names %>%
  glimpse()
```

## Demographics
```{r, demographics4}
mean(study4$age)
sd(study4$age)
table(study4$gender)
```

## Create categorical variable for conditions
```{r, categorical4}
# Agency
study4$agency <- factor(study4$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(study4$agency)
table(study4$agency)
# Decision
study4$decision <- factor(study4$decision, labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(study1$decision)
table(study4$decision)
```

## First-person judgment of imagining how Alex would feel
### Moral Culpability: Means, SDs and ANOVA
```{r, moral4}
# mean and sds
group_by(study4, study4$agency) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study4, study4$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
group_by(study4, study4$agency, study4$decision) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean = mean(moral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(moral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# anova
moral4dv.aov <- aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = study4)
Anova(moral4dv.aov, type = "III")
# effect size
etaSquared(moral4dv.aov, type = 3, anova = TRUE) 
# post hoc scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(moral ~ agency*decision, data = study4), method = "scheffe", 
            conf.level = .95)

# plot
Moral4Plot <- ggplot(study4, aes(x=decision, y=moral, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
Moral4Plot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Programming Type", y = "Moral Culpability", fill = "Agency", 
       title = "Moral Culpability") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```

## Load data in long format
```{r, data4long4}
study4within <- read_csv(here::here("moralstudy4withinresp.csv")) %>%
  clean_names %>%
  glimpse()
```

## Categorical Long Format Data
```{r, categoricallong4}
# Agency
study4within$agency <- factor(study4within$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(study4within$agency)
table(study4within$agency)
# Decision
study4within$decision <- factor(study4within$decision, 
                                labels = c("Deontological", "Utilitarian"))
is.factor(study4within$decision)
table(study4within$decision)
# Perspective
study4within$persp <- factor(study4within$persp, labels = c("Field", "Observer"))
is.factor(study4within$persp)
table(study4within$persp)
```

## Mixed Effects Regression
```{r, withinreg4}
# mixed effects regression
Withresp<-lmer(wresp ~ agency*persp*decision + (1|response_id), data = study4within)
summary(Withresp)

# posthoc test scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(wresp ~ persp*decision, data = study4within), method = "scheffe", 
            conf.level = .95)

# plot
PerspPlot <- ggplot(study4within, aes(x=persp, y=wresp, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
PerspPlot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Perspective", y = "Evaluation of Responsiblity", fill = "agency", 
       title = "Effects of Perspective and Agency on Evaluations of Responsibility") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```

# Experiment 5: COVID scenarios

## Load data
```{r, data5}
study5 <- read_csv(here::here("5covid.csv")) %>%
  clean_names %>%
  glimpse()
```

## Demographics
```{r, demographics5}
# age
mean(study5$age)
sd(study5$age)

# gender
table(study5$gen)
```

## Codes are identical from previous studies, but decisions are re-defined
### Decision (0: Stricter measure or "Keep closed", 1: Looser measure or "Reopen")

## Make categorical variables
```{r, categorical5}
# Agency
study5$agency <- factor(study5$agency, labels = c("Low Agency", "High Agency"))
is.factor(study5$agency)
table(study5$agency)
# Decision
study5$decision <- factor(study5$decision, labels = c("Strict", "Lenient"))
is.factor(study5$decision)
table(study5$decision)
# Scenario
study5$scenario <-factor(study5$scenario, labels = c("Scneario1", "Scenario2"))
is.factor(study5$scenario)
table(study5$scenario)
```

## Check the percentage of strict vs. lenient option in each condition
```{r}
# By agency
```

```{r, alphathree5}
culpability <- as.matrix(cbind(study5$responsible, study5$guilty, study5$regret))
psych::alpha(culpability, keys=NULL,cumulative=FALSE, title=NULL, max=10,na.rm = TRUE,
             check.keys=TRUE,n.iter=1,delete=TRUE,use="pairwise",warnings=TRUE,n.obs=NULL)
```

```{r, means5}
  )
group_by(study5, study5$decision) %>%
  summarise(

  )
group_by(study5, study5$scenario) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),

  )
group_by(study5, study5$agency, study5$decision) %>%

  )
```

## ANOVA for moral culpability
```{r, moral5}
# anova
moral5dv.aov <- aov(moral ~ agency*decision*scenario, data = study5)
Anova(moral5dv.aov, type = "III")
# effect size
etaSquared(moral5dv.aov, type = 3, anova = FALSE) # Effect size
# post hoc scheffe
PostHocTest(aov(moral ~ agency*decision*scenario, data = study5), method = "scheffe", 
            conf.level = .95)

# plot
Moral5Plot <- ggplot(study5, aes(x=decision, y=moral, fill=agency, group=agency)) 
Moral5Plot + 
  stat_summary(position="dodge", geom = "bar") +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  stat_summary(position= position_dodge(width = .9), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3) + 
  labs(x = "Policy Type", y = "Culpability", fill = "Agency", 
       title = "Feelings of Culpability about Policy Implementation") + 
  theme(legend.position = "top") + 
  ylim(0,7) +
  theme_minimal() + apatheme +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_economist()
```
